questions.question: Does your repository support OAI-PMH?
questions.description: Checks whether the repository exposes a working OAI-PMH endpoint.
questions.recommendation: Expose and validate a public OAI-PMH endpoint that supports incremental harvesting.

questions.question: Does your repository metadata support a widely used application profile?
questions.description: An application profile is a set of policies and metadata guidelines for describing scholarly documents. Examples include Dublin Core, OpenAIRE Guidelines and RIOXX. Ensuring the use of a well-known application profile means that publication metadata is described consistently and accurately. Repository content should also expose a minimal set of metadata, including title, abstract, authors and publication year or year of first visibility.
questions.recommendation: CORE metadata indexing requires Dublin Core as a minimum, supports OpenAIRE Guidelines and recommends RIOXX version 3. Repositories should use RIOXX v3 as the preferred metadata application profile for institutional scholarly research outputs and follow the CORE Data Provider Guide.

result.reason: The RIOXX aggregation did not return basic compliance counts.

questions.question: Do you support a tool for tracking COUNTER-compliant downloads?
questions.description: Describes how repository usage statistics are measured.
questions.recommendation: Use a COUNTER-compliant service such as IRUS.

answer.answer: The repository uses IRUS to collect and report COUNTER-compliant download statistics.

questions.question: Does your repository support FAIR Signposting?
questions.description: Checks repository resources for recognised Signposting Link headers.
questions.recommendation: Expose cite-as, describedby, type, author and licence link relations.

questions.question: Do your metadata use COAR vocabularies?
questions.description: Checks harvested metadata for COAR vocabulary identifiers.
questions.recommendation: Use COAR access-right, resource-type and version vocabularies.

questions.question: Does your repository support persistent management of records?
questions.description: Describes identifiers, versioning, withdrawals and long-term links.
questions.recommendation: Use persistent identifiers and publish versioning and withdrawal policies.

answer.answer: Repository records use persistent identifiers. Updates and withdrawals preserve metadata records, version history and stable landing-page URLs.

questions.question: Is your repository configured for the OAI resolver and does it work?
questions.description: Checks whether OAI identifiers resolve to repository landing pages.
questions.recommendation: Configure and test the repository OAI identifier-to-landing-page mapping.

questions.question: Does your repository metadata contain DOIs?
questions.description: Measures repository records containing DOI persistent identifiers.
questions.recommendation: Expose DOIs in standard, machine-readable metadata fields.
